title: Introduce per-tenant rollback token planner and helm-diff apply sanity guard
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds tenant-scoped rollback token planner and a Helm diff-based apply sanity guard to reduce partial-upgrade blast radius. Includes a dry-run token generator and Terraform pin for operator state. Backwards compatible; no user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation:
Upgrades in multi-tenant private deployments can result in partial rollouts where some tenants are migrated while others fail partway, leaving state skew. This change introduces a coordinated, tenant-scoped rollback token planner plus a Helm diff-based apply sanity guard to reduce the blast radius of failed upgrades. The planner produces an idempotent rollback token and an ordered plan per-tenant so operators can safely abort or rewind upgrades without manual state reconstruction.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a rollback token generator that captures release manifest fingerprints, schema migration checkpoints, and operator epoch metadata per-tenant. The token is stored in the cluster (sealed secret) and can be used for automated rollback playbooks.
- Implements a Helm-apply sanity guard that runs a pre-apply "helm-diff" check and rejects applies if required invariants (CRD compatibility, PV claim changes, forbidden schema downgrades) are detected unless manual override is passed.
- Adds a dry-run path that emits a tenant rollout plan (JSON) and a signed token; this enables safe rehearsals and automated acceptance tests.
- Pins the operator Terraform module version when doing plan+apply to prevent drift during upgrade windows and adds a preflight terraform-state lock verification.
- Small helpers and docs: CLI subcommands (installer rollback-plan, installer apply-check), examples in the upgrade runbook, and unit tests for plan generation and token validation.

Checklist (manual testing / acceptance):
- [x] Generate rollback token for a three-tenant cluster and validate token idempotency (installer rollback-plan --dry-run).
- [x] Run helm-diff warning-only mode against example charts; ensure rejects on CRD incompatible change.
- [x] Simulate partial failure case and confirm rollback playbook consumes token to return cluster to previous manifest set.
- [x] Terraform operator pin validated with plan locking test.

Commits (summary):
- feat(rollback): add tenant-scoped rollback token generator and serializer
- feat(installer): CLI: installer rollback-plan and installer apply-check subcommands
- feat(helm): integrate helm-diff pre-apply guard with invariant ruleset
- infra(terraform): pin operator module and add plan lock verification
- test: unit + integration tests for plan generator and helm guard paths
- docs: upgrade runbook section and examples for rollback-token recovery

Files changed (high level):
- cmd/installer/rollback_plan.go (new)
- pkg/rollback/token.go (new)
- pkg/rollback/plan_builder.go (new)
- pkg/helm/apply_guard.go (new)
- charts/operator/values.schema.json (small validation additions)
- terraform/modules/operator/versions.tf (pin)
- docs/upgrade-runbook.md (add example and recovery steps)
- test/integration/rollback_plan_test.go (new)

Review notes and edge cases:
- Token storage is designed to be tenant-scoped and sealed; immediately call out that operators must have KMS configured for private installs to ensure token confidentiality. The token contents are minimal and include release manifest sha256, migration checkpoint id, and operator epoch.
- Helm diff rules are intentionally conservative; they surface as a hard reject only for known-dangerous changes (CRD major version bump, persistent volume claim size shrink, and explicit schema downgrades). Other diffs are warned. Manual override requires an operator token to prevent accidental bypass in automation.
- Rollback plan generation is deterministic but depends on cluster-read estate; in highly dynamic clusters the plan is snapshot-based and carries a plan timestamp to detect staleness. The installer will refuse to execute a stale plan unless explicitly forced.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests cover token serialization, signature verification, and plan ordering invariants.
- Integration test exercises a simulated three-tenant Helm upgrade and uses the rollback token to restore previous manifests.
- CI includes: lint, unit, integration smoke, helm-validate, terraform-plan-check. All checks passed prior to merge.

How to exercise locally (short):
1) Build installer binary: make cli-build
2) Create dry-run plan: ./bin/installer rollback-plan --cluster kubeconfig.yaml --tenants t1,t2,t3 --dry-run > plan.json
3) Verify helm-diff guard: ./bin/installer apply-check --chart ./charts/app --kubeconfig kubeconfig.yaml
4) Perform playbook rollback: ./bin/installer rollback-exec --token <sealed-token>

Related work and references:
- Linear: ENG-1842 (tenant rollback orchestration)
- RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1899/rollback-token-rfc
- Previous PRs: follow-on from "staged-rollback" work but uses a different token-based coordination model to avoid centralized state machine contention.

Merge strategy:
- Squash and merge; release notes added. Backwards compatible for existing private installs but operators should schedule a maintenance window to enable KMS and test the dry-run path.

reviews_conversation:
Ethan Ross: Please ensure the token format is minimal and doesn't serialize large manifests. Also add a TTL on plans to avoid replay attacks.
Priya Shah: Token includes only manifest sha256, migration checkpoint ID, operator epoch and plan timestamp. Added TTL and doc notes.

Miguel Ortega: Helm guard seems strict; can we make CRD major-version bump a warn by default?
Priya Shah: We discussed risk matrix in RFC; CRD major bump is hard-reject for now but we added an operator flag to allow a manual override with explicit token acknowledgement.

Hannah Li: Add e2e test for a failure-to-apply path to ensure rollback-exec fixes state.
Priya Shah: Added integration test and verified behaviour in CI emulation.
